properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB - (SO115) Bldg 2212 Wellhouse
properties.Problem_Description:
A "Waste material" sample collected from under a diesel UST on 7/6/92 gave 120 ppm TPH.  Another 'waste material' sample of soil from wellhouse tank Bldg. 2212 indicates 271 ppm TPH.  A large number of unanswered questions regarding this site are discussed in the correspondence by Gibler to Col. Murray, mid-Jan. 1993.(rpltr4)

Site updated 5/28/2021:
A 118-gallon gasoline (leaded) UST was installed at the site in 1952 and was removed in 1990. Reportedly, 18 cubic yards of contaminated soil was excavated to a depth of 6 ft and was thermally remediated. Samples taken in the excavation indicated BTEX below detection limits, and TPH exceeding the 100 pm cleanup level at the time at concentrations of 120 and 271 mg/kg (ppm?). Additionally, no groundwater samples were collected and lead was not sampled for. In 1993, ADEC recommended additional soil sampling for BTEX, GRO, and lead, although it appears this sampling never occurred. 

In 2013, the ADEC Contaminated Sites Program determined that closure was incomplete, and the ADEC and EPA RPMs requested that the site be investigated. Monitoring wells are recommended for this site. The site has active LUCs/ICs that requires prior approval to work at the site and/or disturb soil, and soil and groundwater use restrictions. The site is currently slated for a Phase II Source Evaluation in 2021.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB - (SO113) Wellhouse Bldg 3408
properties.Problem_Description:
A large number of unanswered questions about this site are discussed in the correspondence by Gibler to Col. Murray, mid-Jan. 1993.(rpltr4)

Site updated 5/27/2021. Site SO113 (Building 3408 UST) is located on Eielson AFB at 550 Division Street, in the central developed portion of Eielson AFB, at the location of the former boiler plant. A 200-gallon UST containing leaded gasoline was historically present at the site and was removed in 1990. 

A closure letter dated April 2, 1993 documents the closure of a 200-gallon Leaded Gasoline UST at Building 3408, EAFB. A UST removal summary was provided by the Air Force on March 18, 1993 that samples were taken in the excavation at the tank fill end and the opposite sidewall in 1990, with TPH levels of 147.6 and 92 mg/kg, and BTEX below detection limits. A total of 111 cy of soil was removed to a depth of 10 ft and no groundwater was encountered. The closure document stated the TPH analyses were only marginally above ADEC present cleanup guidelines, and the source of the contamination and the highly contaminated soil was likely removed and remediated. The closure letter was based upon a limited number of soil samples and levels observed may not be the greatest levels at the site. Handwritten notes on the closure indicate this tank is in the vicinity of Well A, one of the base's primary water supply wells.

ADEC records from 2013 of Eielson LUST Site Closure reviews indicate Bldg 3408 was an incomplete closure due to groundwater never being sampled, insufficient characterization data, and insufficient remediation descriptions including no confirmation sampling. 

Air force records indicate soil samples reportedly contained total petroleum hydrocarbons at concentrations exceeding ADEC cleanup levels. The location of the soil samples could not be confirmed. No groundwater data are available. Additionally, there is no evidence that sampling was performed for lead. 

In 2013, the ADEC Contaminated Sites Program determined that closure was incomplete, and the ADEC and EPA RPMs requested that the site be investigated. The site has active LUCs/ICs that requires prior approval to work at the site and/or disturb soil, and soil and groundwater use restrictions. The site is currently slated for a Phase II Source Evaluation in 2021.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB - (SO117) Bldg 1302
properties.Problem_Description:
Level C cleanup level acceptable (<5 ft to subsurface water, mean annual precipitation < 15 inches, coarse grained soils with fines, no known well within 1 mile, volume of contaminated soil approx. 25 cu.yds.)      Tank removed during June of 1994

Update 8/11/2021: Site reopened.

The Building 1302, SO117 LUST site is located within the Missile Maintenance compound and is adjacent to the IC/LUC buffer zones of source areas SS533 and SO524. Eielson records indicate a 5,000 gallon UST containing diesel that was removed in 1994, however ADEC and 1994 AGRA Summary Report for Tank Closure indicate the tank was 2,000 gallons. The site was listed as closed on 11/01/1999 via email correspondence from the Storage Tank Program, the Closure Notice is dated May 1994, and the August 1994 Summary report for Tank Closure recommended a final closure ruling for the site however no closure letter was drafted. Analytical samples of the stockpiled soils ranged from 1,900 mg/kg to 8,600 mg/kg for DRO, and soil samples from the base of the excavation (6.5 to 8.5 feet bgs) indicated DRO at 550 mg/kg, below the Level C standards at the time but above the current soil MTG CULs. No groundwater samples were collected, and is believed to be present at 9 ft bgs. In 2013 the ADEC Contaminated Sites Program determined the Closure was incomplete, and the ADEC and EPA RPMs requested additional investigation of the site. The site has active LUCs/ICs that requires prior approval to work at the site and/or disturb soil, and soil and groundwater use restrictions. The site is currently slated for a Phase II Source Evaluation in 2021.

properties.Site_Name: NANA Oilfield Services Tank Farm
properties.Problem_Description: During liner replacement activities in September 2010, petroleum-contaminated soil was discovered beneath Tank 3 at the NANA Oilfield Services tank farm on Block 303, Lot 1 of the Deadhorse Airport.  Site investigation activities in April 2011 determined that GRO, DRO, and xylenes were present above DEC cleanup levels.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB (SS521) Bldg 1161 Flightline Ave CITS
properties.Problem_Description:
Petroleum contamination at Eielson AFB former Building 1161 (currently 2615 Flightline Ave) from an unknown source.  Monitoring well 1 is 50 feet north of Bldg 1161, MW-2 is 100 feet east of Bldg 1161 and upgradient of MW-1. 

The 2005 Final Site Characterization Report describes soil and groundwater sampling. RRO has been detected in MW-1 up to 3.51 mg/L, above DEC cleanup levels; total xylenes and DRO were also detected in MW-1 but at concentrations below DEC cleanup levels. RRO, DRO, and total xylenes were detected in MW-2 at levels below DEC cleanup levels. All soil concentrations to date are below DEC cleanup levels.  RRO concentrations are qualified due to lack of quality control testing.

Chromatograms have been used in attempting to show biogenic interference as a source of sampling results, but have proven inconclusive to date.

Update 2022
A construction project for the site encountered Pentachlorophenol (PCP), Perfluorooctanesulfonic Acid (PFOS), Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) and Trichloroethene (TCE) above applicable DEC cleanup levels in surface soils (0-2 feet) on the site.

properties.Site_Name: Point Barrow POW-M Dewline Site Air Terminal Area (SS003)
properties.Address_1: Point Barrow Long Range Radar Station
properties.Problem_Description: The Air Terminal Area (USAF ERP Site SS003) is located north of the main installation on the western shore of the North Salt Lagoon. Data collected during the 2007 Remedial Investigation indicated volatile petroleum hydrocarbons were present in surface soil, surface water of a tundra pond, and in active layer water.  No soil contaminants exceeded 18 AAC 75.341 Tables B1 and B2 Arctic Zone cleanup levels. The single surface water sample from the pond detected TAH at 58.7 mg/kg, which exceeds the Alaska Water Quality standard TAH of 10 mg/kg.  Sheen was also noted on the water.  No documented spills have occurred at the the Air Terminal Area.  The source of contamination is believed to be multiple large historic fuel spills located up-gradient on the adjacent United States Navy (USN) property at the Barrow Naval Arctic Research Laboratory (NARL) Airstrip Site.  The dominant form of contaminant transport appears to occur in the form of dissolved petroleum hydrocarbons moving n the saturated zone above the permafrost.  Active layer water in this area flows west to east  from the adjacent USN property boundary toward the North Salt Lagoon.  Multiple soil removal actions, product recovery activities, and investigations have been conducted on the up-gradient NARL Airstrip Site on the USN property.  The USN is conducting long-term monitoring of the contaminant sources on their property; it is likely to take a a number of decades for remaining contamination at the USN site to attenuate sufficiently to allow unrestricted use.

properties.Site_Name: Point Barrow POW-M Dewline Site Radome Area (SS002)
properties.Address_1: Point Barrow Long Range Radar Station
properties.Problem_Description: The Radome Area is located within USAF ERP Site SS002.  Four distinct source areas at the main installation are located within SS002: the Vehicle Maintenance Area, the Vehicle Fueling Station Area, the Radome Area, and the Transformer Stand Area.  The Radome Area is located below the radome at the west end of Module Train A.  It encompasses the gravel pad in the vicinity of the stairs leading from the west end of the radome.  In 2007, PCBs were detected in the soil at the Radome Area at 2.65 mg/kg.  An estimated 25 cubic yards of soil contain PCB concentrations greater than 1 mg/kg.

properties.Site_Name: Point Barrow POW-M Dewline Site Transformer Stand Area (SS002)
properties.Address_1: Point Barrow Long Range Radar Station
properties.Problem_Description: The Transformer Stand Area is located within USAF ERP Site SS002.  Four distinct source areas at the main installation are located within the IRP site designated as SS002: the Vehicle Maintenance Area, the Vehicle Fueling Station Area, the Radome Area, and the Transformer Stand Area.   The Transformer Stand is located adjacent to the south side of Module Train B, west of the catwalk connecting the two module trains.  From leaks or spills, and estimated 16 cubic yards of soil contain PCBs above the Method Two cleanup level of 1 mg/kg.

properties.Site_Name: Point Barrow POW-M Dewline Site Vehicle Fueling Station Area (SS002)
properties.Address_1: Point Barrow Long Range Radar Station
properties.Problem_Description: The Vehicle Fueling Station Area is located within USAF ERP Site SS002.  Four distinct source areas at the main installation are located within the IRP site designated as SS002: the Vehicle Maintenance Area, the Vehicle Fueling Station Area, the Radome Area, and the Transformer Stand Area. The Vehicle Fueling Station is a former gasoline fueling station located northeast of the garage and on the eastern edge of the gravel access road.  It previously contanied two 6,000 gallon above-ground storage tanks labeled as containing gasoline.  The tanks were in use from 1957 to the 1980's.  Gasoline was dispensed over the gravel pad.  An estimated 70 cubic yards of soil contain xylenes above the Method Two arctic zone cleanup level.

properties.Site_Name: NAPA Auto Parts
properties.Problem_Description: On May 26, 2011, a fire consumed the NAPA Auto Parts store and warehouse located at 1937 Van Horn Road in Fairbanks.  Water and foam sprayed on the building during firefighting efforts acted as a transport mechanism to carry hazardous materials across the paved parking lot to adjacent properties.  Hazardous materials included oil, grease, lubricants, glycols, solvents, paint, and batteries.  An initial response was conducted however, product continued to migrate from the building into adjacent soils.  An assessment conducted by the responsible party's environmental consultant concluded that product weeping from the building would be contained in the porous soils underneath the building and later be removed during the building demolition process.  Grossly contaminated soils from adjacent properties were removed and stockpiled on site until later disposal at OIT.  A site characterization, including groundwater investigation, was conducted to determine the extent of remaining contamination.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB (SS083) Bldg 3240 R-11 Parking Lots
properties.Problem_Description:
Site SS083 consists of a paved lot north of Building 3240 that is used for temporary parking of R-11 refueling trucks.  Building 3240 is an indoor heated parking facility for the refuelers. The west end of the building contains a maintenance shop and office space. No fuel tanks are currently located at the site; however, two 90-gallon ASTs used to store diesel fuel were previously located near the site. One AST was located on the northwest side of Building 3240 and the other AST was located at the west end of Building 3240. It is unknown when these two ASTs were removed.

Stained surface soil was discovered on 8 July 2011 during the re-pavement of the lot north of 
Building 3240.  A total of four areas were identified as potentially impacted using a 
photoionization detector (PID) to field screen soil; three areas were located in the middle of the parking lot and one area was located adjacent to Building 3240 near the former AST. Excavation of the impacted areas began on or before 19 July 2011.  Soil was also excavated at the site during three additional soil removal events which took place 26- 28 September 2011, 4 October 2011, and on an unknown date after 4 October 2011.

Throughout removal activities, the soil was segregated into two categories: (1) soil deemed to be clean and (2) soil deemed to be impacted. Soil deemed to be clean was returned to excavated areas. Fresh soil from an on-base source was used to bring excavated areas to grade. 

Approximately 770 cubic yards of impacted soil was removed during excavation.  Impacted soil was temporarily stored at three locations on Eielson AFB prior to disposal: (1) adjacent to Building 3242, (2) Containment Cell #1, and (3) Containment Cell #2. On 28 September 2012, discreet samples were collected from the impacted soil stored at these locations to characterize the soil for disposal.  The contaminated soil was removed from the site on 13 October 2012 for transportation to Organic Incineration Technology, Inc. located in Moose Creek, Alaska for thermal treatment.

Updated Conceptual Site Model (2025 Remedial Action Construction Report): 
The COCs for soil at Site SS083 Area 3 are POL related compounds GRO, DRO, benzene, ethylbenzene, naphthalene, xylenes, 1,2- dibromoethane, 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene, 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene, and 1-methylnaphthalene. 
The COCs for groundwater at Site SS083 Area 3 are POL-related compounds GRO, DRO, benzene,
ethylbenzene, toluene, naphthalene, xylenes, 1,2-dibromoethane, 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene, 1-
methylbenzene, 2-methylbenzene, and lead, and non-POL-related compounds 1,1,2-TCA and
2-hexanone. Exposure media and pathways at Site SS083 Area 3 are dermal exposure to and
ingestion of contaminated soil (surface and subsurface) and groundwater, inhalation of tap
water vapor, and inhalation of indoor and outdoor air. Current and future receptors for soil,
groundwater, and air media include commercial and industrial workers, construction workers,
and site visitors or trespassers. Future receptors include hypothetical residents. The area is not used for recreation, hunting, subsistence, or farming.

properties.Site_Name: Alyeska PS 06 Former Fire Training Area
properties.Address_1: Pump Station 6; Alyeska Pipeline MP 355; Mile 55 Dalton Highway
properties.Problem_Description: In 2014, the former fire training area at Pump Station 06 (aka Yukon Response Base) was decommissioned. Soil above the liner was excavated and stockpiled. Soil samples from this stockpile contained PFOS above ADEC cleanup levels. in 2017, this soil was transported to OIT for thermal remediation. In 2019, soil samples collected 3 feet below ground surface at the former fire training area footprint and analyzed for PFAS contained PFOS above ADEC cleanup levels.

properties.Site_Name: Alyeska PS 10 Former Fire Training Area
properties.Address_1: Pump Station 10; Alyeska Pipeline MP 586; Mile 218 Richardson Hwy
properties.Problem_Description: In 2015, the former fire training area at Pump Station 10 was decommissioned. Soil above the liner was temporarily stockpiled in a segregated stockpile on the pad in accordance with the  Stockpile Management Plan (EN-21-01). Samples were collected from the excavated soil above the liner and below the liner and analyzed for petroleum fractions, VOCs, PAHs, PFOS, and PFOA. Note: all non-essential structures were removed in 2019.

properties.Site_Name: Tesoro Northstore #76
properties.Problem_Description: This property has been location of a gas station since 1995.  Gasoline contaminated soil and groundwater were identified during UST system closure site assessment work performed in October, 2014.

properties.Site_Name: City of Fairbanks Regional Fire Training Center Burn Pit
properties.Problem_Description: In 2014 a site investigation was conducted associated with the closure of the burn pit (a.k.a. combustible liquids pit) at the Fairbanks Regional Fire Training Center.  The pit was constructed in 1987 and used for firefighting exercises for about 20 years.  These exercises consisted of filling the pit with water, adding fuel (jet, diesel and/or gasoline) to float on water and then igniting and extinguishing fires.  The pit is reported to have not been used for about 10 years.  The pit can be identified from satellite imagery as a circular feature and is reported about 40 feet in diameter with a concrete rim, 2 feet of gravel, and a liner. To prepare the pit for decommissioning, samples were collected from standing water and sediment in the pit. Petroleum and perfluorinated compounds were detected in water.  DEC recommended collection further characterization data before determining disposition of the contents of the pit as PCBs were reported as non-detect at elevated reporting limits and the solid material was not analyzed for perfluorinated compounds (PFCs).  PFCs were detected in the water samples collected from the pit. DEC recommended further site characterization to include sampling of soil and groundwater for petroleum and PFCs.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB (SS107) F35A Flight Simulator Bldg
properties.Address_1: Intersection of Central Avenue and Flightline Avenue
properties.Problem_Description: In May, 2015 contaminated groundwater was encountered during environmental site assessment activities in preparation for construction of the F35A Flight Simulator Building (EIE365).  The source of the suspected petroleum contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB (SS062) Garrison Slough Fire Training Areas
properties.Address_1: E of Building 4335 and to the W of Garrison Slough
properties.Problem_Description:
This site is adjacent to SS037. A utilidor at SS037 was investigated in 1998 after workers complained of negative health impacts from working in the utilidor (see Eielson AFB Administrative Record #483). Investigation of the utilidor included interviewing Base personnel familiar with land use in the nearby areas to identify potential contaminant release locations and types. Those interviews identified three areas to the east of Building 4335 (Facility 2936) where fire training activities took place.  The interviewees indicated petroleum products and unidentified chemicals were applied to burn pits and the ground, lit on fire, and then extinguished by firefighters. 

UPDATE 12-29-2021
The Air Force is investigating the site for PFAS contamination as site: 107.38.175 EAFB AFFF Area #9 Fmr Fire Training Areas Near Entomology Bldg 4335 (FT092).

properties.Site_Name: Kulis ANG - Basewide PFAS
properties.Address_1: 6000 Air Guard Road; Former Kulis Air National Guard Base
properties.Problem_Description:
Confirmed perfluorinated compounds (PFCs) released during KULIS Air National Guard Base (ANGB) operations (1955-2011). Aqueous film forming foam (AFFF), containing PFCs, was used at the former Kulis ANGB for extinguishing petroleum fires and in fire suppression systems at several of the installation buildings. Based on the research conducted, ten potential AFFF areas were identified at former Kulis ANGB and may potentially require further action. 

Soil and groundwater are confirmed to be contaminated with PFCs above cleanup levels. Groundwater is contaminated in one monitoring well. 

While not listed on the NPL, investigation at the former Kulis Air National Guard Base must follow CERCLA process per E.O. 12580 [e.g. CERCLA Sections 104(a), (b), and (c)(4), 113(k), 117(a), and (c), 119, and 121) with respect to releases or threatened releases where either the release is on or the sole source of the release is from any facility or vessel under the jurisdiction, custody, or control of their departments. These functions must be exercised consistent with CERCLA Section 120 Federal Facilities. 

State laws. -- State laws concerning removal and remedial action, including State laws regarding enforcement, shall apply to removal and remedial action at facilities owned or operated by a department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States when such facilities are not included on the National Priorities List. The preceding sentence shall not apply to the extent a State law would apply any standard or requirement to such facilities which is more stringent than the standards and requirements applicable to facilities which are not owned or operated by any such department, agency, or instrumentality.].

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB (SS304P) Bldg 1348 Corrosion Control
properties.Problem_Description: This site was identified in 2015 when it was reported that during corrosion control activities completed in Building 1348 (Facility 538), including sandblasting of components, potentially-contaminated used blast media was habitually dumped in two locations to the north of the building, reportedly over the course of several years.  Contaminants have not yet been confirmed.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB Polaris Lake AFFF
properties.Address_1: SE Shoreline of Polaris Lake; ~0.13 mile E of Bldg 4870
properties.Problem_Description: On August 11, 2016 during an Eielson Air Force Base Fire Department training exercise, an internal pump component of a fire suppression system failed releasing approximately 0.25 gallons of Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) concentrate to the southeast end of Polaris Lake and adjacent shoreline.  Approximately 20 cubic feet of water and 250 square feet of shoreline were affected.  Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) were detected in surface water samples at levels of 16.6-19 ppt and 85.4-249 ppt, respectively. On October 3, 2016, DEC received analytical results for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) sampling in Polaris Lake following an Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) release.  Sample results were taken from the top, middle, and bottom sections of the Polaris Lake water column.  The results for the top section of the water column are 16.6 parts per trillion (ppt) PFOA and 249 ppt PFOS.  The results for the middle section of the water column are 18.5 ppt PFOA and 183 ppt PFOS.  The results for the bottom section of the water column are 19.0 ppt PFOA and 85.4 ppt PFOS.  Soil surrounding Polaris lake was also sampled for PFOA and PFOS did not have a detection.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB Bldg 1300 AFFF
properties.Address_1: Combat Alert Cell (CAC) Building 1300; 277 Caragain Road
properties.Problem_Description:
This site includes multiple releases, including:

Spill no. 16309908901: On March 29, 2016 at 2:05PM, a malfunction of the fire suppression system at Eielson Air Force Base Building 1300 triggered the suppression system to come on, releasing Buckeye Hi-Ex aqueous film forming foam (AFFF). The generators did not come on and so the foam was not aerated and was released as a solution into the building. It was estimated that 100 gallons of AFFF mixed with water was released inside the building for a total of approximately 4,500 gallons of solution. The liquid leaked out of the building, onto the pavement outside, and further onto soil. The material safety data sheet indicates it does not contain Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS). DEC performed a site visit on March 30 and observed puddles with sparse white foam and milky liquid on the parking lot pavement, as well as the ground adjacent to the pavement. DEC requested that soil samples be taken from the ground where foam puddles were observed during the site visit and test for perfluorinated compounds. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) was confirmed in soil above DEC cleanup levels.

Spill no. 16309927902:  On October, 5, 2016, while testing pumps on a truck that had recently received maintenance, AFFF was accidentally released onto the pavement at Building 1300.  Approximately 270 gallons of a mixture of foam concentrate and water (approximately 1:3 ratio) were released.  Inactive potable water well no. 7 is 250 feet from the spill site.

properties.Site_Name: Alyeska PS 05 Former Fire Training Area
properties.Address_1: MP 137 Dalton Highway; MP 274.4 Alyeska Pipeline
properties.Problem_Description: In 2016, the former fire training area at Pump Station 05 was decommissioned. Prior to decommissioning activities, three pre-excavation samples were collected from the soil and analyzed for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS). All three soil samples contained PFOA above ADEC method two migration to groundwater cleanup levels (note: all soil samples were considered biased low due to holding time exceedance).  Eight cubic yards of soil above and below the liner were excavated and stockpiled. This stockpile contained PFOA above ADEC method two migration to groundwater cleanup levels and was transported to OIT as part of a pilot test burn in 2017. In 2018, drinking water samples collected from the well head contained PFOS up to 0.0237 ug/L and PFOA up to 0.0738 ug/L. This sample result it above the EPA Lifetime Health Advisory level, but below the ADEC Table C groundwater cleanup levels. Soil samples collected from the fire training area contained PFOA and PFOS contamination above the ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup levels. The PS 05 drinking water well is located 3,800 feet away from the fire training area adjacent to Jim River. The drinking water well groundwater is 48 feet below ground surface.

properties.Site_Name: Alyeska PS 07 Former Fire Training Area
properties.Address_1: Near MP 42 Elliott Highway; MP 414.2 Alyeska Pipeline
properties.Problem_Description: In 2016, three pre-excavation soil samples were collected and analyzed for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS). The PFOA samples were non detect. The PFOS samples contained concentrations up to 0.00010 mg/kg, which is less than the DEC cleanup level (note: all soil samples were considered biased low due to holding time exceedance). In 2017, the former fire training area at Alyeska Pump Station 07 was decommissioned. Contaminated soil was excavated and confirmation soil samples collected from the bottom and sidewalls of the excavation and analyzed for petroleum fractions, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and volatile organic compounds. None of these soil samples contained contaminant concentrations above ADEC cleanup levels. Note: the onsite drinking water well is 76 feet bgs about 1,500 feet upgradient from the former fire training area. This PFOS/PFOA contaminated drinking water well is being tracked as another site known as: Alyeska PS 07 Sitewide PFAS (see file 330.38.145 for more info).

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Ft. Rich AFFF Area #04 Fire Station 5 Bldg 48010
properties.Address_1: Eastern Side of Bryant Army National Guard Airfield
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #4 is located at Fire Station 5 Building 48010 on the eastern side of the airfield at Bryant Army National Guard Airfield Station (JBER-Richardson). Soil results from a site inspection specifically for aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E and JBER-R detected perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) below EPA risk-based screening levels and ADEC human health cleanup level, but above the ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup level.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS135P AFFF Area #06 C-17 Debris Storage Yard

properties.Problem_Description:
AFFF Area #6 is located on the southeastern corner of Gibson Avenue and 9th Street on JBER-Elmendorf. Plane parts that were covered with an AFFF blanket during the 2010 C-17 crash response were transported to this area.

Groundwater results from a site inspection specifically for aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E and JBER-R detected the presence of perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS136P AFFF Area #07 Current AFFF Spray Test Area
properties.Address_1: South and West of 23rd Street, North of Fighter Drive, E of Fairchild Avenue
properties.Problem_Description:
AFFF Area #7 is located south of the western end of the flightline, south of
23rd Street. All current AFFF spray testing for the emergency response vehicles at JBER-E is conducted at this location. Soil results from a site inspection specifically for aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E and JBER-R detected perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) above ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup levels but below EPA Risk based screening levels. 

Groundwater results for PFOS and PFOA were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels in crossgradient and downgradient monitoring wells. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS137P AFFF Area #08 Corrosion Control Hangar Bldg 6263
properties.Address_1: South of Main Flightline on Gibson Avenue
properties.Problem_Description:
AFFF Area #8 is located south of the main flightline on Gibson Avenue at JBER-E. It was
built in 1944, is used for F-15 exterior paint maintenance, and is equipped with an aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) fire-suppression system. A site inspection conducted at the site found groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS138P AFFF Area #09 Current Fire Training Area
properties.Address_1: ~0.3 Mile E of Northern End of Flightline; N of 31st Street; E of Declaration Drive; W of Railroad Tracks
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #8 is located approximately 0.3 mile east of the northern end of the flightline at JBER-E. It currently consists of a circular, lined burn area protected by a berm, and is surrounded by gravel roads, parking lots, a mock building, and an onsite pump system. A site inspection detected soil results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) detected during a site investigation of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R were above ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup levels but below EPA risk-based screening levels and ADEC human health levels. properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #12 is located on the west ramp of the JBER-E flightline. Groundwater results for PFOS and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Extent of contamination is unknown.

Site inspection soil results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) detected during a site investigation of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R were above ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup levels but below EPA risk-based screening levels and ADEC human health levels. Groundwater results for PFOS were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf AFFF Area #15 Fire Station 7 Bldg 14431

properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #15 is located on the northern side of the flightline on JBER-E. Fire Station 7 serves the flightline and houses one emergency response vehicle. Site inspection soil results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) detected during a site investigation of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R were above ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup levels but below EPA risk-based screening levels and ADEC human health levels. Groundwater results for PFOS and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS145P AFFF Area #19 Hangar 6 Bldg 9311
properties.Address_1: S of Main Flightline Tward Northern End of Jerstadt Avenue
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #19 is located on JBER-E south of the main flightline toward the northern end of Jerstadt Avenue. It was constructed in 1944 and the Alaska National Guard operates the Army’s Regional Flight Center within this hangar. During a site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) were above EPA health advisory levels and ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) was above the EPA health advisory level. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS146P AFFF Area #21 Hangar 10 Bldg 15444 & 15455
properties.Address_1: 30th Street on Taxiway Kilo; Northern Side of Main Flightline
properties.Problem_Description:
AFFF Area #21 is Hangar 10 located on JBER-E on the northern side of the main flightline, on Taxiway Kilo. Hangar 10 was built in 1957 as a heavy aircraft fuel maintenance hangar and is the home of the 176th Air National Guard. Building 15455 (fka 42-400 Floor Drains & IS-1 Maint. Dock Hangar 10) is Hangar 10 an Building 15444 (fka 42-401 Water Pump Station) is a support building and the CERCLA source area. Bldg. 42-400 (Hangar No. 10) has been used for fuel loading operations. Past spills, up to 1,300 gallons, have occurred at the facility. The building floor drains discharge into dry wells in gravelly soil at each end of the building (Engineering-Science, 1983).

In the past, most of the fuel flowed into floor drains and, hence, into dry wells
at each end of the building (Engineering-Science, 1983). The floor drains discharge to oil-water separators (Ritz, USAF, personal communication, 08 March 1989). 

During a 2016 site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were above EPA health advisory levels, but not above the ADEC groundwater cleanup levels.  Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS147P AFFF Area #22 Hangar 16 Bldg 15658
properties.Address_1: Taxiway Foxtrot; Northern Side of Main Flightline; W of Talley Avenue; S of Hangar 17 (Bldg 16670)
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #22 is Hangar 16 located on JBER-E on the northern side of the main flightline, on Taxiway Foxtrot. It was constructed in 1945 and is the home of the F-22 Combat Alert Cell. The hangar consists of eight separate bays in a single line. During a site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) was above the EPA health advisory level, but not above the ADEC groundwater cleanup levels.  Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS148P AFFF Area #23 Hangar 17 Bldg 16670
properties.Address_1: Taxiway Foxtrot; Northern Side of Main Flightline; W of Talley Avenue; N of Hangar 16 (Bldg 15658)
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #23 is Hangar 17 located on JBER-E on the northern side of the main flightline on Taxiway Foxtrot. It was constructed in 1945 and is the home of the F-22 Combat Alert Cell. The hangar consists of eight separate bays in a single line. During a site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) were above the EPA health advisory level, but not above the ADEC groundwater cleanup levels. Soil results were above the ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup level, but below the ADEC human health cleanup level and the EPA health advisory level. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS155P AFFF Area #24 Hangar 18 Bldg 17470
properties.Address_1: Taxiway Joker; Northern Side of Main Flightline
properties.Problem_Description: AFFF Area #24 is Hangar 18 located on the northern side of the main flightline on Taxiway Joker and is the home of the 176th Air National Guard. Built in 1999, this is a large aircraft maintenance hangar with an AFFF fire suppression system. During a site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, soil results were detected perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) below the EPA risk based screening level and ADEC human health level, however, above the ADEC migration to groundwater cleanup level. Groundwater results for PFOS were above the EPA health advisory level and the ADEC groundwater cleanup level. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) was detected above the EPA health advisory level but below the ADEC groundwater cleanup level. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Elmendorf SS150P AFFF Area #26 UC-35A Cessna Crash Location
properties.Problem_Description: The exact location of AFFF Area #26, the UC-35A Cessna crash, is unknown. On October 6, 2009, a Cessna UC-35A (Cessna 560 Citation V Ultra) crashed in the central portion of the JBER-E east-west runway. The approximate location is on the southern side of Airlifter Drive, which is a paved area directly on the flightline. During a site inspection of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) areas on JBER-E & JBER-R, groundwater results for perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were above the EPA health advisory level, but below the ADEC groundwater cleanup level. Extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB F35A R11 Fuel Truck Shelter
properties.Address_1: S of Loop Taxiway; N of ST20 (E7); W of ST20 (E9)
properties.Problem_Description: Soil samples were collected in April 2017 as part of an evaluation for the construction project EIE388 at the proposed location for the F35A R11 fuel truck shelter at Eielson Air Force Base.  Initial photoionization detector field screening results were less than 20 parts per million, but laboratory results confirmed perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), dichloroethylene (DDE), and ethylene dichloride (1,2-DCE) were present in soil above DEC cleanup levels. The source and extent of contamination is unknown.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB Basewide (AKA Sitewide) PFAS
properties.Problem_Description:
This database record includes general information about per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) contamination at Eielson Air Force Base (EAFB) and Moose Creek.  PFAS are a diverse group of compounds that have been used in many industrial applications and consumer products including fire-fighting foams.  Ongoing investigations are gathering information to determine the location of PFAS-contaminated sites on EAFB. Upon completion of the investigations, specific areas may be assigned individual Hazard IDs and tracked separately.  Please see site-specific database entries to learn more about an individual EAFB PFAS-contaminated site.

Update 2025
This database record will continue to provide updated Action entries regarding the EAFB remedies and studies to address PFAS related  groundwater impacts both on the base and in adjacent communities (Moose Creek and North Pole).

24309915103: Spill of 5 gallons of PFAS containing IDW water released at the PFAS Wastewater Treatment. Will be tracked under CS.

properties.Site_Name: Galena AFS/Airport CG109 AFFF Release Areas
properties.Problem_Description:
The Galena AFS/Airport CG109 AFFF (Aqueous Film Forming Foam) Areas site is comprised of areas where the per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) have been detected.  The following areas were identified during a 2016 Site Investigation at the Former Galena Forward Operating Location (FOL): Area 1 - Fire Protection Training Area (FT001); Area 3 - Building 1549 (Old Fire Station); Area 4 -  Building 1556 (Fire Station); Area 5 - Building 1573 (Vehicle Maintenance Facility); and Area 9 - Sanitary Sewer System. The State of Alaska, Department of Transportation and Public Facilities owns AFFF Areas 1, 3, 4, and 5. The City of Galena owns AFFF Area 9 (Sanitary Sewer System). Further investigation is required to delineate the extent of contamination and evaluate potential risks.

The approximate locations of the five AFFF Areas are listed below:
AFFF Area 1: Fire Protection Training Area (FT001) 64°44'15.72"N, 156°54'24.48"W - AFFF Area 1 is tracked under Site FT001 (Hazard ID 555)
AFFF Area 3: Building 1549 (Old Fire Station)  64°44'20.5"N, 156°57'17.5"W
AFFF Area 4: Building 1556 (Fire Station) 64°44'20.99"N, 156°57'2.46"W
AFFF Area 5: Building 1573 (Vehicle Maintenance Facility) 64°44'22.60"N, 156°57'5.97"W
AFFF Area 9: Sanitary Sewer System 64°44'28.46"N, 156°57'22.45"W

properties.Site_Name: ADOT&PF Barrow Airport Sitewide PFAS
properties.Problem_Description: Concern over the use of aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) as a fire retardant in the Barrow (Utqiagvik) community led to the sampling of Isatkoak Reservoir, the drinking water source for the community. Multiple surface water samples were collected across the extent of the reservoir, with the greatest concentration repeatedly detected at a collection point near the eastern end of the runway, where the airstrip meets the western edge of the reservoir. Two surface water samples collected one month apart from this location, yielded water concentrations significantly elevated above other samples, indicating that a source of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) contamination is likely on the Alaska Department of Transportation and Public Facilities (ADOT&PF) Airport property.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB F35A OSS/Weapons/Intel Facility
properties.Address_1: S of Flightline Avenue (Innter Loop), ~465 Ft W of Intersection w/Central Avenue
properties.Problem_Description: In March 2017, during soil investigation activities (EIE385) in the proposed location for the Eielson Air Force Base F35A OSS/Weapons/Intel Facility, petroleum and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) contamination was confirmed in soil above DEC cleanup levels.  The source and extent of contamination has not been determined.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB F35A Bldg 4280 ADAL FTD Facility
properties.Address_1: 2871 Flightline Avenue; Eastern Side of Building 4280
properties.Problem_Description:
UPDATE 
Between August 2017 and June 2019, excavation for F-35 construction project EIE 377 generated approximately 2,200 cubic yards of PFOS and PFOS + POL contaminated soil which was stockpiled at a location on LF003 at Eielson.  Confirmation sampling indicted PFOS contamination of soils remains at the site.  Confirmation  samples confirmed DRO, trimethylbenzenes, ethylbenzene, xylenes,
naphthalene, and methylnaphthalenes above DEC cleanup levels. The highest DRO level was identified in the Trench Valve sample (DRO = 43,100 mg/kg).

Multiple areas of contamination have been discovered within the boundaries of construction project EIE377 - F35 A Bldg 4280 ADAL (add to and alter) FTD (field training detachment) facility.  Diesel range organics and arsenic have been confirmed above DEC cleanup levels.

The site includes the following spills:

Spill no. 17309924403; spill date = 9/1/17; substance = unknown; quantity = unknown; source = broken flange on abandoned fuel line; PRP file no. 107.02.004; description: Abandoned fuel line unearthed during construction project EIE377, contaminated soil was segregated based on field screening results and stockpiled on site.

Spill no. 17309925402; spill date = 9/11/17; substance = unknown; quantity = unknown; source = unknown; PRP file no. 107.02.004; description:  sheen on standing water within construction project EIE377, contaminated soil was segregated based on field screening results and stockpiled on site.

properties.Site_Name: FIA - Sitewide PFAS
properties.Problem_Description: Fairbanks International Airport (FIA) detected Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in groundwater and surface water samples taken at various locations throughout airport property in September 2017. Concentrations of contaminants exceeded the EPA's lifetime health advisory (LHA) levels and DEC cleanup levels in several samples. The contaminants originate from the historic use of Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) in the vicinity of the Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting building (ARFF) on the west side the facility and the Firefighter Training Areas on the south side of the facility; groundwater concentrations of PFOS and PFOA in samples taken near these locations exceed concentrations of samples from other areas.

properties.Site_Name: Eielson AFB F35A Squad Ops/AMU & Propulsion MX/Dispatch Hangars
properties.Address_1: Loop Circle; N of Bldg 1335; NE of Bldg 1338
properties.Problem_Description:
UPDATE
During the 2018 - 2019 construction season, several thousand cubic yards of PFOS contaminated soil was excavated and stockpiled for treatment or disposal.  PFOS contamination was identified in all excavation bottom confirmation samples indicating PFOS remains in soil and groundwater on the site. 

In the fall of 2017, petroleum contamination was discovered during construction of two hangers at Eielson Air Force Base:  project EIE376 for the F35A Propulsion MX/Dispatch Hangar, and project EIE379 for the F35A Squad Ops/AMU Hangar.  Diesel range organics, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, volatile organic compounds, per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances have been confirmed in soil and a petroleum sheen was noted on groundwater entering excavated areas.

The site includes the following spills:

Spill no. 17309926401; spill date = 9/21/17; substance = unknown; quantity = unknown; source = unknown; PPRP file no. 107.02.004; description: soil that exceeded field screening limits during construction project EIE376 for the F35A Propulsion MX/Dispatch Hangar were excavated and stockpiled according to work plan.

Spill no. 17309929102; spill date = 10/18/17; substance = unknown; quantity = unknown; source = unknown; PPRP file no. 107.02.004; description: during construction project EIE379 for the F35A Squad Ops/AMU Hangar a sheen and smell were present on groundwater during excavation for building footers. Soil from the footer excavation was stockpiled in accordance with the work plan.

Spill no. 18309919201; spill date = 4/1/18; substance = water containing PFOA and PFOS; quantity = 270,000,000 gallons (3 million/day for 90 days); source = dewatering discharge; PPRP file no. 107.02.004; description: dewatering activities from foundation preparation area (64.656136, -147.03559) for F35A project EIE376 Hanger Propulsion Maintenance Building caused the discharge contaminated water to an area of ~50 acres behind the E-11 tank farm (64.650937, -147.043958).  Surface water samples collected from settling ponds at culvert by Quarry Road exceeded 0.4 ug/L.

properties.Site_Name: JBER-Ft. Rich AFFF Area #03 Fire Station 4 Bldg 654
properties.Problem_Description: Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) Area #03 is located on the western side of Sixth Street, and serves as the main fire station on JBER-Richardson. It is surrounded by a paved/concrete area with small grassy areas bordering to the northwest and southeast. Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) were detected in the soil and PFOA was detected in the groundwater during an EPA site inspection (SI) of AFFF areas which includes AFFF #03. The purpose of the SI was to determine the presence or absence of PFOS & PFOA. Extent of contamination is unknown.  Data quality is being evaluated to determine if contaminants exceed DEC cleanup levels.
